root_cause.text: The `zero_vruntime` tracking was not updated during context switches for runnable tasks (removed from `put_prev_task`/`set_next_task` paths by a previous fix), leaving only tick and full enqueue/dequeue to advance it, which caused vruntime to become stale and overflow under rapid yield scheduling.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description states that “All that moves zero_vruntime are tick and full {de,en}queue” and that the prior commit removed updates from `__{en,de}queue_entity()` calls in `{put_prev,set_next}_task()`. The fix adds `avg_vruntime(cfs_rq)` to `update_deadline()` (called at slice expiration) and modifies `yield_task_fair()` to use `update_deadline()`, ensuring zero_vruntime is updated at the end of every slice.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces avg_vruntime as the virtual time reference for EEVDF, but avg_vruntime is only updated in __enqueue_entity and __dequeue_entity via avg_vruntime_add/sub. There is no update to avg_vruntime in the context switch code (put_prev_task/set_next_task), which are not shown in this diff but implicitly remain unchanged from earlier code. This means that when a runnable task is preempted and later continues, its vruntime is updated via update_curr, but avg_vruntime is not updated accordingly, causing the lag calculation to become stale. This matches the root cause: the zero_vruntime tracking (equivalent to avg_vruntime) is not updated during context switches, which can lead to vruntime overflow under rapid yield scheduling. The fix (updating avg_vruntime during context switch) is absent in this commit.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit b3d99f43c72b56cf7a104a364e7fb34b0702828b
Author: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org>
Date:   Mon Feb 9 15:28:16 2026 +0100

    sched/fair: Fix zero_vruntime tracking
    
    It turns out that zero_vruntime tracking is broken when there is but a single
    task running. Current update paths are through __{en,de}queue_entity(), and
    when there is but a single task, pick_next_task() will always return that one
    task, and put_prev_set_next_task() will end up in neither function.
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit diff shows the fix for the zero_vruntime tracking issue. The old `update_zero_vruntime()` function was removed, and `avg_vruntime()` now internally calls `update_zero_vruntime()` to update `cfs_rq->zero_vruntime` (line: `update_zero_vruntime(cfs_rq, delta);` inside `avg_vruntime()`). Additionally, the calls to `update_zero_vruntime()` from `__enqueue_entity()` and `__dequeue_entity()` were removed, and a new call to `avg_vruntime()` was added in `entity_tick()` (line: `avg_vruntime(cfs_rq);`), ensuring zero_vruntime is advanced during ticks even for a single task. This eliminates the stale vruntime and potential overflow described in the root cause.
